title: Foundation models for electricity price forecasting and battery arbitrage: Can they replace market-specific forecasting models?
note: arXiv record, v1 only (2026-08-31), cs.LG and econ.EM, authors Lipiecki and Weron. Nine zero-shot variants from five foundation-model families against two price-forecasting benchmarks in Germany, Poland and Spain, 2021-2025. Says only the TabPFN models beat the benchmarks consistently and significantly; in battery arbitrage the ranking depends on risk tolerance. No code link, no journal DOI.

title: Foundation models for electricity price forecasting and battery arbitrage (full text)
note: Accuracy tables, TabPFN-3 vs DDNN-JSU (MAE / RMSE / CRPS). Germany 12.59 / 22.59 / 9.15 vs 14.58 / 24.96 / 10.70. Poland 13.25 / 21.81 / 9.61 vs 14.97 / 24.70 / 10.96. Spain 11.18 / 17.50 / 8.15 vs 12.66 / 19.07 / 9.30. Chronos-2 CRPS 11.80, 10.74, 9.46. No intervals; significance by one-sided conditional predictive ability tests. Read twice through fetch summaries, same values.

title: Foundation models for electricity price forecasting and battery arbitrage (full text)
note: Setup: day-ahead prices, 24 hourly values a day, zones DE-LU, PL, ES. Test 2021-01-01 to 2025-12-31 (1,826 days). Inputs: day-ahead load and wind/solar forecasts, lagged gas, coal, oil and carbon prices, day of week; no weather. Models: Chronos-2 (3 variants), Moirai-2, TimesFM-2.5, TabPFN-2, TabPFN-3, TabPFN-TS-3, Mitra; benchmarks LEAR+CP and DDNN-JSU.

title: Foundation models for electricity price forecasting and battery arbitrage (full text)
note: Arbitrage, Germany, 1 MWh battery: unlimited bids TabPFN-TS-3 EUR 132,716 vs DDNN-JSU 130,434 (perfect foresight 143,474); quantile strategy at 50%: DDNN-JSU 86,123 vs TabPFN-TS-3 85,416. Benchmarks and tabular models share covariates and a 1,449-observation context; Moirai-2 got prices only, Mitra a shorter context. No pre-registration, code statement or checkpoint ids.
